title: Hummingbirds See Colors That Don't Exist for Humans
subject: broad-tailed hummingbird

scenes.text: Hummingbirds see colors your brain can't picture.
You have three color cones. Birds have a fourth, and it sees ultraviolet.
Scientists tested wild hummingbirds in the Colorado Rockies, with over 6,000 feeder visits.
The birds told ultraviolet plus green apart from plain green, though the scientists saw no difference.
Mixed colors like that are called nonspectral. They're not in the rainbow. Humans only get one: purple.
Hummingbirds can see at least four. And we'll never know what they look like.

description:
Hummingbirds see colors your brain can't picture.
Princeton researchers showed wild broad-tailed hummingbirds can tell apart mixed ultraviolet colors that look identical to us.
What color do you wish you could see?
first_comment: If you could see one extra color, what do you think it'd look like?
